events.title: Nathan Hale Is Hanged as a Spy
events.description: Captain Nathan Hale of the Continental Army was caught gathering intelligence on British troops on Long Island. He was hanged in British-occupied New York City. He was 21. His last words are traditionally remembered as a regret that he had only one life to give for his country.
events.significance: Hale became an enduring symbol of patriotism and sacrifice in the American Revolution. He is still celebrated as one of the young nation's first folk heroes.

events.title: Michael Faraday Is Born
events.description: The future physicist and chemist was born in Surrey, England, to a modest family and had little formal schooling. He rose from bookbinder's apprentice to one of the great experimental scientists of his age.
events.significance: Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, which underpins electric generators, transformers and motors. His work helped lay the foundation for the modern electrical age.

events.title: The French First Republic Is Proclaimed
events.description: After the monarchy was overthrown, the National Convention's decision to abolish royalty took effect. The date was later treated as the start of Year I of the French Republican Calendar.
events.significance: The founding of the Republic marked a radical break with centuries of monarchy in France. It shaped the course of the French Revolution and inspired republican movements across Europe.

events.title: Lincoln Issues the Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation
events.description: Days after the Union victory at Antietam, President Abraham Lincoln announced that enslaved people in states still in rebellion on January 1, 1863 would be declared free.
events.significance: The announcement turned the Civil War into a struggle explicitly tied to ending slavery. It paved the way for the final Emancipation Proclamation and the later abolition of slavery in the United States.

events.title: Iraq Invades Iran
events.description: Iraq launched air strikes on Iranian airfields and sent forces across the border, beginning a full-scale war between the two neighbors. The fighting lasted nearly eight years.
events.significance: The Iran–Iraq War was the longest conventional war of the 20th century. It caused enormous casualties and reshaped politics across the Middle East.
